name: Manuel Peters
life: “I still remember sitting in my parked car the first morning I tried driving again.” On Friday, near Studio Boulevard, Manuel waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I was driving the other vehicle. My letter to the family has stayed in the same drawer for eleven months.
appearance: Manuel has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. In conversation Manuel holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Manuel uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Manuel well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To deliver the carefully written letter appropriately.
family: Marlowe May is Manuel’s half-sibling. Manuel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Marlowe leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The broken till*, Marlowe says, “I manage a cashless shop. I want to know why the pencil line moved faster than ours.”
connections: Isaac Jensen. An adult driver's unsent letter and a child's unasked-for statement belong to different memories of one day. Also in the story is Lee Ingram (former collision counterpart).
